about: Kept by bin/kyrie play --keep, or bin/kyrie keep, and played again by test/traces.test.ts: what it came to must be what it comes to.
told: The first brick goes into the hot pool with a sound like a cough. ‘Mind the pipe behind the third course,’ says Maud Veale’s voice, perfectly steady, from the hot side. ‘I know where my pipe is, Veale,’ says Nesta’s, from the other. There is a great deal of dust. In the dust, for the first time in thirty-one winters, two women look at each other through a hole the size of a hat. ‘You have got old,’ says one. ‘So have you, you great fool,’ says the other, and neither says anything else for a long time. Seethe is one hall again by midwinter: a raw-edged hole where the arch was, and a rail across it where Pen can lean. The pointers stand at seven. Nobody has said who closed hers first, and nobody will, and the drovers have taken to calling the hot pool the Maud and the cold the Nesta, which neither of them has been able to stop. Osric Sallis goes up the drove road with his pears, and is back the winter after, by whichever door will have him. The pear is on the stone in the first hard frost. The drove goes down to Brynach on Thursday, with the toll-song, and the Rì’s headsman in it still a hood and a rope. Gethin sings the last verse a little slower than he did. Brother Cuthwin goes on down the drove road in the sleet, still preaching against baths, on his twenty-ninth day, and is heard of at Hafod for a fortnight afterwards, mostly from upwind. Ottoline Brightwell stays the winter in the room over the copper, and is heard singing in the steam in the early mornings, and is not always alone. Pen is out of work. He does not mind. He has been told by both of them to sit down, and he is, for the first time in his life, between. Seethe, in the sleet, smokes at both ends of one roof, and the wall that divides the slates into two colours has a hole in it where, if you stand in the yard on the right night, you can see a lamp pass from one side to the other, carried by somebody with a bad hand. Where the arch was bricked there is a doorway, raw at the edges, with dust still on the water.
